key_insight: World Tracing bridges a key gap in image-to-3D: it keeps 3D geometry aligned with the input image while also hallucinating the parts that are hidden from view. In simple terms, it aims to be both faithful to what you see and complete beyond what you see.
problem_solved: Existing image-to-3D methods usually fall into one of two camps: depth estimators that stay tightly aligned to visible pixels but only recover the front surface, and generative 3D models that produce complete objects but often drift away from the input image. This paper addresses the trade-off between pixel faithfulness and geometric completeness.
method: Introduces a generative pixel-aligned geometry representation called World Tracing.
Predicts 3D points for each input pixel in an ordered stack along the camera space, enabling geometry to extend beyond the visible surface.
Combines image alignment with completion, producing 3D structure that remains anchored to observed pixels while filling in occluded regions.
impact: This is useful for practitioners building reconstruction, AR/VR, robotics, and 3D content generation systems that need both accurate image alignment and plausible full-object geometry. It could improve downstream tasks where partial reconstructions are insufficient, such as manipulation, scene understanding, and editable 3D asset creation.
